get_pull_request.notes:
| Field | |
| --- | --- |
| `pull.files` | The files it changes, with lines added and removed. |
| `checks` | The latest run of the acceptance checks against its head, with each command's output. |
| `overlaps` | Other pull requests in progress that change the same files. |
| `behind` | Whether the default branch has moved since it was made. |
| `landing` | Whether it is being brought up to date to land. |
| `lifecycle` | For a pull request the g1t agent is seeing through: its stage, such as `working`, `checking`, `reviewing` or `needs_you`. |
| `comments` | Comments, reviews and events, with `path`, `line` and `verdict`. |
| `messages` | Messages sent to the agent working on it. |
| `statuses` | Commit statuses reported for its head, such as workflow runs. |
| `mergeable` | Whether it merges cleanly into its target: `clean`, `conflicting`, `checking` (being worked out) or `unknown`. Worked out ahead of time whenever it or its target moves. |
| `conflicts` | When `mergeable` is `conflicting`, the files that conflict. Resolve them by merging the target in, or have the g1t agent do it. |
| `earlierChecks` | Earlier runs of the acceptance checks, newest first, without their output. |

Checks are started by g1t, not through the API. They run when a pull request becomes ready for review and again when its head moves.

get_pull_request_changes.notes: A file's `status` is `added`, `modified` or `deleted`. A binary file has no `hunks`. In a line, `old` is `null` when it was added and `new` is `null` when it was deleted.
